outcome.rationale: The SAPIEN M3 early feasibility study is predicted to demonstrate positive outcomes based on: (1) established Edwards SAPIEN platform technology adapted for mitral position, (2) appropriate patient selection for early feasibility, (3) published TMVR feasibility study benchmarks showing technical success 85-92% and MR reduction 85-94%, (4) iterative device development allowing procedure optimization across 72 patients. Primary technical success and secondary MR reduction endpoints are both predicted to be met. Key risks are anatomical complexity of native TMVR, learning curve effects, and longer-term durability unknowns. Trial designed for feasibility rather than definitive efficacy, making success threshold achievable.

analysis_trace.finding: NCT03230747 is an Early Feasibility Study (EFS) of the Edwards SAPIEN M3 System for transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) in high-risk patients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR ≥3+). Single-group design with 72 enrolled patients. Status is ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING with expected primary completion June 2021.
Mitral regurgitation (MR) in patients at high risk for cardiovascular surgery. The SAPIEN M3 is a novel TMVR system consisting of a dock and valve designed for native mitral valve replacement.

High-risk surgical candidates with MR ≥3+, NYHA class ≥II, LVEF ≥30%, hemodynamically stable on heart failure medication. Exclusions include severe MAC with LVOT obstruction risk, prior mitral intervention, mechanical aortic valve, and significant comorbidities. Population represents typical early feasibility TMVR cohort.

The SAPIEN M3 system uses a two-component design: a dock implanted first to create a landing zone, followed by implantation of a balloon-expandable SAPIEN valve. This design addresses anatomical challenges of native TMVR including annular sizing and LVOT obstruction risk.

Primary endpoint (primary-0): Technical Success is a composite requiring: alive, successful access/delivery/retrieval, correct device deployment, and freedom from emergency surgery/reintervention. This is assessed at procedure end. Secondary endpoint (secondary-0): MR reduction to 0 or 1+ at 30 days, assessing functional efficacy.

Evidence from systematic reviews of early TMVR experience (JAHA 2019 systematic review, JACC 2019 feasibility studies) indicates technical success rates of 85-92% for dedicated TMVR devices in early feasibility studies. The SAPIEN platform has extensive safety data from TAVR applications. For MR reduction, published 30-day data from TMVR feasibility studies show MR ≤1+ achievement in 85-94% of patients with successful implant. The M3 system's dock design aims to improve deployment stability and reduce paravalvular leak.

Key safety considerations include: LVOT obstruction (mitigated by dock design and patient selection), device embolization/migration, access complications (transapical or transfemoral), bleeding, and procedural mortality. Early feasibility studies typically exclude highest-risk anatomies to optimize initial experience.

Primary risks to technical success: anatomical challenges (severe MAC, small LVOT), delivery system navigation difficulties, device malposition requiring retrieval. Secondary risks: suboptimal MR reduction due to paravalvular leak or device underexpansion. 30-day mortality and complications affect secondary endpoint assessment.

Primary-0 prediction based on: (1) Edwards' extensive TAVR experience with SAPIEN platform, (2) early feasibility study design selecting favorable anatomy, (3) published TMVR technical success rates of 85-92%, (4) 72-patient sample allowing iterative learning. Predicted technical success probability 0.88. Secondary-0 prediction based on: (1) device mechanism replacing native valve eliminates primary MR, (2) 30-day MR reduction rates of 85-94% in TMVR literature, (3) dock design intended to optimize valve positioning. Predicted MR reduction probability 0.86.

Limited direct evidence for SAPIEN M3 specific outcomes as this is the early feasibility study. Most available literature covers other TMVR devices (Tendyne, Intrepid, EVOQUE) or valve-in-valve procedures. Full-text retrieval failed for key articles, limiting access to exact numerical benchmarks. No gold standard randomized data available for native TMVR at time of prediction.

analysis_trace.finding: NCT03230747 is an Early Feasibility Study (EFS) of the Edwards SAPIEN M3 System for transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) in high-risk patients with severe mitral regurgitation (MR ≥3+). Single-group design with 72 enrolled patients. Status is ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING with expected primary completion June 2021.
Mitral regurgitation (MR) in patients at high risk for cardiovascular surgery. The SAPIEN M3 is a novel TMVR system consisting of a dock and valve designed for native mitral valve replacement.

High-risk surgical candidates with MR ≥3+, NYHA class ≥II, LVEF ≥30%, hemodynamically stable on heart failure medication. Exclusions include severe MAC with LVOT obstruction risk, prior mitral intervention, mechanical aortic valve, and significant comorbidities. Population represents typical early feasibility TMVR cohort.

The SAPIEN M3 system uses a two-component design: a dock implanted first to create a landing zone, followed by implantation of a balloon-expandable SAPIEN valve. This design addresses anatomical challenges of native TMVR including annular sizing and LVOT obstruction risk.

Primary endpoint (primary-0): Technical Success is a composite requiring: alive, successful access/delivery/retrieval, correct device deployment, and freedom from emergency surgery/reintervention. This is assessed at procedure end. Secondary endpoint (secondary-0): MR reduction to 0 or 1+ at 30 days, assessing functional efficacy.

Evidence from systematic reviews of early TMVR experience (JAHA 2019 systematic review, JACC 2019 feasibility studies) indicates technical success rates of 85-92% for dedicated TMVR devices in early feasibility studies. The SAPIEN platform has extensive safety data from TAVR applications. For MR reduction, published 30-day data from TMVR feasibility studies show MR ≤1+ achievement in 85-94% of patients with successful implant. The M3 system's dock design aims to improve deployment stability and reduce paravalvular leak.

Key safety considerations include: LVOT obstruction (mitigated by dock design and patient selection), device embolization/migration, access complications (transapical or transfemoral), bleeding, and procedural mortality. Early feasibility studies typically exclude highest-risk anatomies to optimize initial experience.

Primary risks to technical success: anatomical challenges (severe MAC, small LVOT), delivery system navigation difficulties, device malposition requiring retrieval. Secondary risks: suboptimal MR reduction due to paravalvular leak or device underexpansion. 30-day mortality and complications affect secondary endpoint assessment.

Primary-0 prediction based on: (1) Edwards' extensive TAVR experience with SAPIEN platform, (2) early feasibility study design selecting favorable anatomy, (3) published TMVR technical success rates of 85-92%, (4) 72-patient sample allowing iterative learning. Predicted technical success probability 0.88. Secondary-0 prediction based on: (1) device mechanism replacing native valve eliminates primary MR, (2) 30-day MR reduction rates of 85-94% in TMVR literature, (3) dock design intended to optimize valve positioning. Predicted MR reduction probability 0.86.

Limited direct evidence for SAPIEN M3 specific outcomes as this is the early feasibility study. Most available literature covers other TMVR devices (Tendyne, Intrepid, EVOQUE) or valve-in-valve procedures. Full-text retrieval failed for key articles, limiting access to exact numerical benchmarks. No gold standard randomized data available for native TMVR at time of prediction.

Percutaneous Transseptal TMVR System in Patients Not Eligible For Surgery or TEER Oct 27, 2025 ACC News Story Print Font Size A A A On this page: Resources Percutaneous transseptal mitral valve replacement (TMVR) using the SAPIEN M3 system effectively reduced mitral regurgitation (MR) with low rates of complications and mortality in patients who were not candidates for conventional surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER), according to results of the ENCIRCLE trial presented at TCT 2025 and simultaneously published in The Lancet . The trial involved a total of 287 patients from the U.S., Canada, Europe, Israel and Australia who had MR ≥3+, NYHA Class ≥II, and were unsuitable for surgery or TEER due to clinical, anatomic or technical considerations. The balloon-expandable, dedicated SAPIEN M3 mitral transcatheter heart valve was implanted in each patient and follow-up was conducted at 30 days, six months and one year. In overall findings, the primary endpoint – the composite of all-cause mortality and rehospitalization for heart failure at one year compared to a pre-specified performance goal of 45% – was 25.2%. All-cause death and heart failure hospitalization rates were 13.9% and 16.7%, respectively. Additionally, improvements in MR grade were observed across all patients, with more than 95% having ≤1+ total MR at 30 days and one year. Researchers also noted the TMVR system had a procedural safety profile similar to TEER and that patients experienced clinically meaningful and durable improvements in symptoms and quality of life. \"Percutaneous transseptal TMVR had a low mortality rate while providing a significant reduction in [MR] severity and providing meaningful and durable improvements in functional status and quality of life,\" said David Daniels, MD . \"These findings will help guide clinical practice by providing an alternative treatment option for patients who are not suitable for conventional surgery or TEER procedures.\" Additionally, Daniels and colleagues say their findings could allow for \"future reintervention with percutaneous transseptal mitral valve-in-valve implantation in the event of structural valve deterioration,\" noting that \"reintervention after failed TEER remains a major limitation.\" Resources TCT 2025 Meeting Coverage Clinical Topics: Invasive Cardiovascular Angiography and Intervention, Valvular Heart Disease, Interventions and Imaging, Interventions and Structural Heart Disease, Angiography, Nuclear Imaging Keywords: Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics, TCT25, Angiography, Heart Valve Diseases You must be logged in to save to your library.
